info.name: Vault Run — RGS B2B Integration
info.description:
Runnable Postman collection for integrating the **Vault Run** crash-game Remote Game Server (RGS) into an online-casino platform via the **seamless-wallet** model.

Authoritative source: `docs/api-integration-spec.md` (v1.0). Every route, header, body, and field here is derived from that spec and the production controllers (`src/operator/`, `src/wallet/`, `src/game/`, `src/fairness/`, `src/common/`). All money values on the wire are **integer minor units** (spec §8): `100` = €1.00 for EUR.

**Convention (spec §0):**
- Routes prefixed `/api/...` are **exposed by the RGS** — you call them (folders 1–4).
- Routes with no `/api` prefix (`/bet`, `/win`, `/rollback`, `/balance`) are **exposed by YOU, the operator** — the RGS calls them. Folder 5 lets you fire example requests at your own wallet to confirm it speaks our protocol.

**Setup:**
1. Import this collection AND `vaultrun-sandbox.postman_environment.json`, then select the environment (top-right).
2. Fill the secret-ish variables: `launchSecret`, `reportingKey`, `walletApiUrl`, `walletApiKey` (placeholders are present; replace with the values we issue you).
3. Run **1. Operator — launch & session → POST /api/operator/launch** first: its pre-request script mints a signed launch JWT into `{{launchToken}}`, and its test script saves the returned session token into `{{sessionToken}}` for every other authenticated request.

**WebSocket:** the live game protocol is Socket.IO (spec §6). Postman's Socket.IO request type is a GUI/app construct that is not part of the importable Collection v2.1 JSON schema, so folder 6 is a **documentation-only stub**; the full, copy-pasteable Socket.IO usage (handshake auth, emits, listeners) is in `postman-collection-guide.md`.

**Status:** the wire contract is implemented and stable; production currently runs operator-mode OFF (internal play-money demo). The hosted operator-mode sandbox is **live** at `https://sandbox.vaultrun.app` (integration testing only — not under the production SLA); point `baseUrl`/`wsUrl` at it. Keep the `*.vaultrun.example` placeholders in request examples and do not hardcode any production hostname (spec §14).

item.name: 1. Operator — launch & session
item.description:
The signed launch protocol (spec §4/§5). You mint a short-lived HMAC-SHA256 launch JWT with your `launchSecret`, the client posts it to `POST /api/operator/launch`, and the RGS returns a **session (play) token** used for the WebSocket handshake. Closing the session is a logout.

The `POST /api/operator/launch` request includes a **pre-request script** that mints the launch JWT for you (so you don't need a server) and a **test script** that captures the session token into `{{sessionToken}}`.

exec: // Mint a launch JWT (HMAC-SHA256) signed with {{launchSecret}} and store it in {{launchToken}}.
// Mirrors src/operator/launch-token.service.ts: claims operatorId, playerId, currency,
// demo:false, jti (unique, one-time), iat, exp = iat + 120 (TTL_SECONDS = 120). See spec §4.
// Uses Postman's built-in CryptoJS — no external deps.
// base64url of a CryptoJS WordArray (used for the HMAC signature bytes)
// RFC4122 v4 uuid for the one-time jti
console.warn('launchSecret is not set — set it in the environment before launching.');
console.log('Minted launch JWT (jti=' + payload.jti + ', exp in 120s).');
// Capture the session (play) token for every other authenticated request + the WS handshake.
try { data = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { /* non-JSON error body */ }
pm.test('response has a session token', function () {
console.log('Saved sessionToken (currency=' + data.currency + ', decimals=' + data.decimals + ', sessionId=' + data.sessionId + ').');

request.description:
Open the game from a launch token (spec §5). **No auth header** — the launch JWT in the body is the credential.

The **pre-request script** mints the JWT into `{{launchToken}}` (HMAC-SHA256 over `header.payload` with `{{launchSecret}}`; claims `operatorId`, `playerId`, `currency`, `demo:false`, unique `jti`, `iat`, `exp=iat+120`). The **test script** saves `token` (the session/play token) into `{{sessionToken}}`.

**Body:** `{ "token": "<launch JWT>" }`. `token` must be ≥ 10 chars else **400** `invalid_body`; a failed verification is **401** with the error string (`invalid_launch_token`, `unknown_operator`, `currency_not_allowed`, `demo_not_allowed`, `launch_token_already_used`).

**200 response fields:** `token` (session token → WS `auth.token`), `sessionId`, `walletId`, `currency`, `decimals`, `locale`, `callbackUrl`. Session-token TTL defaults to 4 h. See spec §4, §5, §12.

Close (revoke) the caller's session(s) — a logout (spec §5). Authenticated by the player's **own** session token (`Authorization: Bearer {{sessionToken}}`).

Soft-revokes every live `GameSession` bound to that wallet: the token can no longer reconnect or bet, while in-flight settlements still resolve. A guest (no session-bound wallet) is a no-op.

**200 response:** `{ "ok": true, "revoked": 1 }`.

item.name: 2. Player (session-token auth)
item.description: Player read-only endpoints authenticated by the **session token** (`Authorization: Bearer {{sessionToken}}`), captured by the launch request (spec §13.2). In operator mode the balance is the **operator's authoritative balance** (fetched via your `/balance`); the transactions list is our **local reconciliation journal**, not the player's authoritative statement.

request.description: Returns `{ currency, balance }` (balance in minor units). In operator mode this is **your authoritative balance** (resolved via your `POST /balance`), not our journal. Requires a valid session token. See spec §13.2.

Returns our **local ledger journal** (last 50 rows: `id, type, amount, balanceAfter, refType, refId, createdAt`). In operator mode this is a **reconciliation aid**, not the player's authoritative statement (which lives at the operator). See spec §13.2.

item.name: 3. Operator reporting (reporting-key auth)
item.description: B2B reporting (spec §13.1), authenticated by your **reporting API key** `Authorization: Bearer {{reportingKey}}` (format `vrk_<operatorId>.<secret>`). Every route is hard-scoped to your `operatorId` (taken only from the key, never from the query). Money is summed in minor units and returned as decimal **strings** (sums can exceed 2^53). Demo bets are excluded unless `includeDemo=true`. Dates accept ISO instants or `YYYY-MM-DD` (date-only snaps to start/end of UTC day).

request.description: Per-currency totals over `[from, to]`: `betCount`, `wagered`, `won`, `ggr`, `uniquePlayers`, `rtp`, `decimals`. Money fields are decimal strings in minor units. See spec §13.1.

query.description: Inclusive end. Range is capped at 366 days.

request.description: The same per-currency totals as `summary`, **bucketed per UTC day**. The date range is capped at 366 days (else **400**). See spec §13.1.

query.description: Optional keyset cursor — pass the previous page's nextCursor (a bet UUID).

request.description: Paginated per-bet rows: `id, roundId, playerId, currency, panel, amount, status, cashoutMult, payout, demo`, timestamps, plus `nextCursor`. Page with `cursor` (a bet UUID) + `limit` (max 200). Key your reconciliation book by `betId` = `id` (spec §10). See spec §13.1.

query.description: Our bet UUID (sent on every wallet call). Provide EXACTLY ONE of betId or transactionId.
Alternative: the idempotency key we sent on a wallet call (URL-encoded) — bet:{roundId}:{userId}:{panel}:debit | bet:{betId}:payout | bet:{betId}:refund | bet:{betId}:restart_refund.

request.description:
Single-transaction status lookup (spec §13.2) — resolve ONE money-move to its disposition when a `/bet` or `/win` response was lost. Reporting-key auth, hard-scoped to your `operatorId`. Provide **exactly one** of `betId` or `transactionId`.

**200** returns the bet's `status` plus `debitState` / `refundState` / `payoutState` (`pending`/`applied`/`reversed` · `none`/`pending`/`applied` · `none`/`pending`/`paid`), `stake`/`payout`/`cashoutMult` (decimal strings), and best-effort `debitTxId`/`payoutTxId`. **Read the disposition from the `*State` fields, never from a single boolean.** A **404** `transaction_not_found` (also returned for another operator's tx and internal/guest play) is **NOT** proof the move didn't occur on your wallet — reconcile by your own dedup, never re-apply on a 404. See spec §13.2.

**Money-WRITE; activation-gated** (per-operator rate-limit + key-scope prereqs before an operator is enabled for void). Fully reverse a **settled** bet so it is as if it never happened — refund the stake, and for a **won** bet also reclaim the payout first (spec §13.3).

Auth: the **reporting API key** (`Authorization: Bearer {{reportingKey}}`, `vrk_<operatorId>.<secret>`); hard-scoped to your `operatorId` and re-checked against `bet.operatorId` — a bet that is not yours → **404** `bet_not_found` (no cross-tenant existence oracle). Path `betId` = our bet UUID (non-UUID → **400** `invalid betId`). **Body:** `{ "reason"?: string }` — optional, logged for audit only (≤500 chars, control chars stripped); the body may be `{}`.

**Status → result:** `busted`/`cashed_out` → **200** `status:"voided"`, `reversed:true`; already `voided` → **200** `reversed:false` (idempotent no-op); `cancelled` → **200** `status:"cancelled"`, `reversed:false`; `active` → **409** `bet_not_settled`; `reserving`/`cancelling`/`payout_pending` → **409** `bet_transient`; lost CAS race → **409** `bet_state_changed`. Idempotent on the bet and resumable. See spec §13.3.

item.name: 4. Public (no auth)
item.description: Public, unauthenticated endpoints (spec §8, §13.5, §13.6). Currency precision, round history/current snapshot, and provably-fair verification. Crash points are never leaked before the crash; a round's seed/salt are disclosed only after its seed is revealed.

request.description: Canonical per-currency precision table: `{ currencies: [{ code, decimals, name }] }`. Cacheable (Cache-Control public, max-age 3600). Use the `decimals` to render minor units. See spec §8.
The last 30 finished rounds: `[{ id, crashMult, endedAt }]`. Use a returned `id` as `{{fairnessRoundId}}` for the fairness round endpoint. See spec §13.5.

Current public round snapshot — `{ roundId, phase, phaseEndsAt, multiplier, serverTime }` (or `{ phase:"waiting", multiplier:1.0 }` when idle). **No crash leak** — only the live climbing multiplier while running. See spec §13.5, §6.2.

The active fairness chain's public commitment (commit hash, epoch, salt source). The crash point for upcoming rounds is bound by this commitment before betting closes. See spec §13.6 and `provably-fair-guide.md`.

Reveal + verification data for a finished round: revealed `seed` + `salt`, `commitHash`, `chainIndex`, `prevSeed`, the on-chain `crashPoint`, the independently `recomputedCrash`, `matches`, and `linkVerified` (SHA256 chain link). If the round's seed is not yet revealed, returns `{ roundId, status, revealed:false }`. Set `{{fairnessRoundId}}` from `GET /api/rounds/history`. See spec §13.6 and `provably-fair-guide.md`.
Public commitments for ALL fairness epochs (chain-of-custody, including exhausted chains). Use an epoch number as `{{fairnessEpoch}}` for the seed dump. See spec §13.6.

Per-epoch **revealed** seed dump for chain-of-custody reconstruction. Never returns an unrevealed (future) seed. `400 invalid_epoch` for a non-integer/negative epoch; `404 epoch_not_found` if unknown. See spec §13.6 and `provably-fair-guide.md`.

Recompute a crash point from a `seed` + `salt` (and optional `prevSeed` for the chain-link check) — exactly what a client can also do offline. Returns `{ crash, linkVerified }`.

**Body:** `{ "seed": "<hex>", "salt": "<string>", "prevSeed": "<hex, optional>" }`. `seed`/`prevSeed` must be hex and `salt` non-empty, else **400**. Fill `seed`/`salt` from a `GET /api/fairness/round/:id` reveal. See spec §13.6 and `provably-fair-guide.md`.

item.name: 5. Operator wallet (YOU implement — examples to test YOUR wallet)
item.description:
**These call the OPERATOR's endpoint, not the RGS.** They target `{{walletApiUrl}}` with `Authorization: Bearer {{walletApiKey}}` and reproduce the EXACT requests the RGS makes on every money move (spec §7). Fire them at your own wallet implementation to confirm it speaks our protocol: correct request shapes, Bearer auth, idempotency on `transactionId`, the `{ operatorTxId, balance }` / `{ balance }` responses, and `402`/`409`/`{error:"insufficient_funds"}` on insufficient funds.

Transaction-id formats (spec §9): stake = `bet:{roundId}:{userId}:{panel}:debit`, payout = `bet:{betId}:payout`, cancel refund = `bet:{betId}:refund`. The same `betId` accompanies the stake, win, and any rollback. **On this operator-wallet contract, `amount` and the response `balance` are integer minor units sent as a BigInt-safe decimal string** (e.g. `"100"`) — parse with BigInt, never Number, since a high-decimal-currency value can exceed 2^53 (spec §8). Reference implementation: `load/operator-wallet-stub.ts`.

Tip: run `/bet` then `/win` then `/balance`, and `/rollback` to undo a debit — your wallet must dedup retries and roll back exactly.

exec: pm.test('200 on a debit that applied (or 402/409/insufficient_funds when out of funds)', function () {

request.description:
**Debit the stake** (spec §7.1). The RGS calls THIS on `place_bet`.

**Body:** `playerId`, `currency`, `amount` (positive minor units, as a **BigInt-safe decimal string** — parse with BigInt, never Number), `transactionId` (`bet:{roundId}:{userId}:A:debit` — dedup on this), `roundId`, `betId`.

**200:** `{ "operatorTxId": "op-987", "balance": "9900" }` (`balance` is a decimal string of minor units). **Insufficient funds:** respond `402`/`409`, or `200/4xx` with `{ "error": "insufficient_funds" }` (a clean rejection, not retried). MUST be idempotent: a retry with the same `transactionId` returns the same result, never double-debits (spec §9).

**Credit the payout** (spec §7.2). The RGS calls THIS on a winning cash-out. Same shape as `/bet`; `amount` is the positive payout (`floor(stake × cashOutMultiplier)`, capped), sent as a **BigInt-safe decimal string**.

**Body:** `transactionId` = `bet:{betId}:payout`. **200:** `{ "operatorTxId": "op-988", "balance": "34155" }` (`balance` is a decimal string of minor units).

A win is **never** rolled back by the RGS; on an unconfirmed `/win` the RGS retries the **idempotent** `/win` (same `transactionId`) and otherwise marks the bet `payout_pending` for its reconciler. **Dedup correctly or you risk double-crediting** (spec §9).

**Undo a named transaction** (spec §7.3). The RGS calls THIS to compensate an ambiguous (timed-out) debit and during stranded-reservation recovery.

**Body:** `transactionId` = the **id of the bet/win being undone** (NOT a new id) — here the stake's `bet:{roundId}:{userId}:A:debit`. **200:** `{ "operatorTxId": "op-989", "balance": "10000" }` (`balance` is a decimal string of minor units).

MUST be **idempotent on its own effect**: if that transaction was applied, reverse it; if it was never applied (or already rolled back), no-op. Either way return the current authoritative balance. It is safe to receive a rollback for a `transactionId` you never saw (spec §9).

**Read the authoritative balance** (spec §7.4). The RGS calls THIS to serve `GET /api/wallet/balance`.

**Body:** `{ "playerId": "{{playerId}}", "currency": "{{currency}}" }`. **200:** `{ "balance": "10000" }` (minor units, as a **BigInt-safe decimal string** — parse with BigInt). Note: unlike the others, this response has **no** `operatorTxId`.

item.name: 6. WebSocket (Socket.IO) — reference
item.description:
**Documentation-only.** The live game protocol is **Socket.IO** (spec §6), not HTTP. Postman's Socket.IO request is a GUI construct that is NOT part of the importable Collection v2.1 JSON schema, so it cannot be encoded here without producing a non-importable artifact. This folder is a reference stub; the full copy-pasteable Socket.IO setup is in `postman-collection-guide.md`.

**Connect** (Socket.IO, NOT a raw WebSocket — Postman: New → Socket.IO):
- URL: `{{wsUrl}}`
- Handshake auth (Settings → Handshake → Auth, or Args): `{ "token": "{{sessionToken}}" }`
- Guests may connect with NO token (read-only round events; money actions return `not_authenticated`).

**Emit (client → server)** — every message gets a Socket.IO ack:
- `subscribe_round` — (no payload) → `{ ok:true }` + re-emits `round_state`.
- `time_sync` `{ "t0": 1750000000000 }` → `{ ok:true, t0, serverTime }`.
- `place_bet` `{ "panel":"A", "amount":100, "autoCashout":2.0 }` → `BetResult`. `panel` ∈ A|B, `amount` finite positive minor units, `autoCashout` finite > 1 (optional).
- `cancel_bet` `{ "panel":"A" }` → `BetResult`.
- `cash_out` `{ "panel":"A" }` → `CashoutResult`.
- `reality_check_ack` — (no payload) → `{ ok:true }` (unblocks bets in RG enforce mode).

**Listen (server → client):** `round_state`, `multiplier_update`, `bet_accepted`, `bet_rejected`, `bet_cancelled`, `cashout_accepted`, `cashout_rejected`, `bet_busted`, `round_crashed`, `round_settled`, `balance_updated`, `reality_check`, `session_time_limit`.

Limits: one active socket per user (a second drops the first); 15 msg/s per socket (`rate_limited`). See spec §6 and the collection guide.

item.name: Socket.IO connect + events (read the description / guide)

request.description:
**Not an HTTP request — do not Send.** This stub documents the Socket.IO connection; create the actual real-time session via Postman → New → **Socket.IO**, connect to `{{wsUrl}}` with handshake auth `{ token: {{sessionToken}} }`, then use the emit/listen events listed in this folder's description.

**Emit examples:**
- `place_bet` `{ "panel":"A", "amount":100, "autoCashout":2.0 }`
- `cash_out` `{ "panel":"A" }`

**Listen for:** `round_state`, `multiplier_update`, `bet_accepted`, `cashout_accepted`, `round_crashed`, `round_settled`, `balance_updated` (and `bet_rejected`, `bet_cancelled`, `cashout_rejected`, `bet_busted`, `reality_check`, `session_time_limit`).

Full walkthrough: `postman-collection-guide.md`. Protocol reference: api-integration-spec.md §6.
